anomalies.observed: R5 is 68k and R6 is 1k3 in the MIC26903 feedback divider. The schematic note states Vout = 0.8*(1+R5/R6). With these values, Vout = 0.8*(1+68/1.3) ≈ 42.6 V.
anomalies.expected: R5 should be 6.8k (or another value that yields approximately 5 V) to match the specified 5 V rail. The schematic note formula and the spec both indicate a 5 V output.

evidence.quote: R5 68k; Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6) (Power sheet, MIC26903 regulator section)

5 V rail: A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V. Design notes on this section: inductor L = 15uH for 5% ripple current; feedback divider relation Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)

anomalies.impact: The buck regulator will attempt to output 42.6 V, but the input is limited to 26 V, so it will run at maximum duty cycle and the 5 V rail will rise toward the input voltage. This will destroy the 3.3 V LDO and any 5 V loads.

anomalies.observed: Both the INA219 current sensor (U1) and the PCA9685 PWM driver (U2) are connected to the same I2C2 bus (I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC) and both are configured for I2C address 0x40.
anomalies.expected: I2C devices sharing a bus must have unique addresses. One of the two devices must be configured to a different address (e.g., INA219 to 0x41, 0x44, or 0x45).

evidence.quote: INA219 note: I2C address: 0x40 (Power sheet); PCA9685 note: I2C address: 0x40 (FCC Peripherals sheet)
Current/voltage sensor ... I2C addr 0x40; PWM/servo driver ... I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The FCC cannot communicate with both devices reliably. I2C transactions will conflict, causing read/write failures or corrupted data on the shared bus.

anomalies.observed: The TMP100 temperature sensor (U6) has ADD0 (pin 5) tied to +3.3V and ADD1 (pin 6) tied to GND. The schematic note and the spec both state the I2C address should be 0x4E.
anomalies.expected: A TMP100 with only two address pins (ADD0, ADD1) can only be set to addresses 0x48, 0x49, 0x4A, or 0x4B. To achieve 0x4E, a different part (e.g., TMP75 with three address pins) or different strapping is required.

evidence.quote: U6 TMP100 note: I2C address: 0x4E; ADD0 tied to +3.3V, ADD1 tied to GND (NAVC Peripherals sheet)
Temperature sensor | NAVCPeripherals | TMP100, I2C addr 0x4E

anomalies.impact: The temperature sensor will not respond at the expected address 0x4E. Software attempting to read the TMP100 at 0x4E will fail.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains three significant anomalies: a 10x error in the 5V buck feedback resistor (R5 = 68k instead of 6.8k), an I2C address conflict between the INA219 and PCA9685 (both 0x40 on the same bus), and a TMP100 address mismatch where the pin strapping cannot produce the stated 0x4E address.
